title: Think Twice before Going for Incentives: Social Norms and the Principal's Decision on Compensation Contracts

scopes.description: Reproduce Figure A1's path analysis for the additional randomized-contract experiment described in the online appendix. The supplied release contains only the appendix PDF and no executable workflow or analysis data.

requirements.description: Author-compatible analysis data or estimation input for Figure A1's path analysis (N = 32), covering the documented contract, perceived norm, perceived trust, and misreport constructs. The appendix supplies results and construct definitions but no input file, schema, identifiers, exclusions, or compatible route.

issues.description: The frozen package inventory contains only cardineals_yin_online_appendix.pdf. The appendix reports Figure A1's path analysis but provides no executable author program or run instructions, so there is no supplied entry point to attempt.

The appendix describes an additional experiment, estimates a QML path analysis with N = 32, and defines its constructs, but does not establish the analysis input format, sample/exclusion handling, full model specification and settings, or executable workflow. Dependency closure and a compatible input route remain unknown.

evidence.description: The frozen work-item inventory lists exactly one package file, the online appendix PDF, and no code or data files.
The appendix identifies Figure A1 as results for an additional experiment with randomly determined contracts.
evidence.quote:
This online appendix reports the results of the additional experiment discussed in Section 4.4
of the manuscript. In this additional experiment, principals cannot decide on the type of
contracts for their agents. The contracts are randomly determined.

evidence.description: Figure A1 reports jointly estimated QML path coefficients and fit statistics for N = 32.
evidence.quote:
Figure A1: This figure shows the results of the path analysis (N = 32). All paths displayed in
this figure are estimated, and they are estimated jointly using quasi-maximum likelihood
(QML) method. The standardized path coefficient and corresponding two-tailed p-value are
shown next to each path. The paths with coefficients significant at the 0.10 level or less are
depicted in solid lines, and other paths are in dotted lines. We calculate goodness-of-fit of this
model using the standardized root mean square of the residual (SRMR). The SRMR of the
model is 0.04; values lower than 0.10 are considered to be favorable (Bentler [1995], Weston
and Gore [2006]).

evidence.description: The appendix gives operational descriptions of the variables used in Figure A1.
evidence.quote:
CONTRACT is the contract received by the subordinates in the Main Stage of this additional
experiment. This variable equals 1 if the contract is the incentive contract and 0 if the contract
is the fixed-salary contract.
PERCEIVEDNORM represents the extent to which subordinates agree that others reported
high costs in the experiment, on a 7-point scale

actions.description: Request the complete author workflow or approved replacement description and the compatible analysis input for the additional-experiment path analysis in Figure A1.
steps: Obtain the executable author program or approved replacement workflow, including the Figure A1 entry point, model specification, estimator settings, and required stages.

Obtain the author-prepared data or exact estimation-input contract for N = 32, including format, variable coding, identifiers, sample/exclusion handling, missing-value treatment, and any transformations.
Map all documented Figure A1 constructs and confirm how the supplied input corresponds to the author's analysis before assessing an execution attempt.
validation: Confirm that the documented input and workflow cover the 32 observations and all Figure A1 constructs, and that the future rerun reproduces the reported path coefficients and SRMR without changing the analysis specification.

review_notes: This assessment covers the frozen package variant whose only inventoried artifact is the online appendix PDF. It reports one additional-experiment path analysis, but provides neither executable code nor the estimation input; no analysis-only scope is supported.
The appendix reports QML estimates and describes the four constructs, while model execution details, the compatible input route, and any necessary preprocessing remain unknown.
No author program was executed, no dataset was read or downloaded, and no software requirement can be established from the supplied release.
